data.content_ref: inline:The target assumes that calibration on the divergence stratum distinguishes genuine reliability from mere compliance, but this is insufficient. A panel could be perfectly calibrated on divergence cases by systematically pegging confidence to checklist coverage (e.g., confidence = proportion of checklist boxes answered) rather than to genuine meta-monitoring. If the checklist's coverage happens to correlate with correctness on those cases, the panel will appear calibrated — confidence tracks correctness — yet the process remains mere compliance with no epistemic insight into when the checklist is unreliable. Calibration alone cannot separate a panel that knows the checklist's reliability boundary from one whose confidence heuristic accidentally co-varies with correctness. The target itself names this confound as a countercondition ('confidence is an artifact of checklist-completion rate') but fails to recognize that calibration analysis cannot rule it out, because a completion-rate-driven confidence will, by construction, produce good calibration whenever completion rate predicts accuracy. The distinguishing evidence the target promises is therefore not delivered.
